log.why: E11 splits the prior probability almost evenly (0.504 vs 0.496), maximizing expected information gain for Ticket 1.
Treating at 30 uM splits the prior probability mass nearly in half (0.620 vs 0.380), maximizing information gain for Ticket 2.
E11 narrowed the culprit to katG, rpoB, or sodA; testing katG directly checks the highest-probability candidate.
E6 (100 µM) directly distinguishes the top two candidates on Ticket 2: 100 µM (0.515) and 300 µM (0.332).
Start incubating E5 on Ticket 3 to split the prior roughly in half while we prepare to publish Tickets 1 and 2.
Test {ompF, rpoB, gyrA} (0.582 prior mass) on Ticket 4 to utilize a free incubator before publishing Tickets 1 and 2.
Test top candidate gyrA (0.454) on Ticket 3 so it incubates while we publish Tickets 1 and 2.
E11 splits Ticket 4's posterior nearly evenly (0.524 vs 0.476), and we can publish Ticket 1 while it incubates.
Ticket 1 has only 4 seconds left and a strong 0.866 posterior for katG after E0 and E11.
Ticket 2 has only 10 seconds left and 300 µM has a strong 0.817 posterior after no response at 30 µM and 100 µM.
Test top candidate trpE directly on Ticket 4 so it can incubate while we publish Ticket 3 next.
GyrA has a strong 0.903 posterior and only 16 seconds remain, leaving no time to run another experiment before expiration.
The posterior for trpE is 0.956 with only 27 seconds remaining, making immediate publication the safest high-value choice.
E1 at 0.3 uM best bisects the prior probability mass (0.398 vs 0.602) for maximum information gain.
While E1 tests <= 0.3 uM, E2 tests <= 1 uM to simultaneously isolate the 1 uM hypothesis or narrow the upper range.
Testing at 3 uM directly distinguishes our leading hypothesis (0.523) from higher dose thresholds before the round ends.
Wait 6s for growing plate E3 on Ticket 5 to finish so we can publish with high confidence before the round ends.
With only 3 seconds left in the round, no experiments can finish, so we attempt to publish Ticket 5 which has a positive expected value.
